# Session Access Checklist: Autonomous build mode in more than one session at the same time

**Purpose**: Review the requirements for per-session autonomous mode, permission-prompt routing, the lock-2 guard, session id path safety, saved machines and two sessions at the same time, before planning
**Created**: 2026-11-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `checklist` procedure based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Access: permission-prompt routing

- [ ] CHK001 Is the rule "a session is on only when its own entry exists" stated once and applied to every reader by name? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Is it stated which id the approve hook compares: the worker's recorded orchestrator id against the entries, not the worker's own id? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the case of a worker whose orchestrator turned off while another session stays on covered, with the result that its prompts are not sent on? [Coverage, Spec §US1 Scenario 4, §US2]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it stated that a session not in autonomous mode sees no change in prompt handling from this feature? [Completeness, Spec §US1 Scenario 4]

## Access: lock-2 guard

- [ ] CHK005 Does the guard requirement cover make, change and remove for both the folder and each entry, by shell command and by edit tool? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK006 Is it stated that the guard keeps its current level (a text match) and that raising it is out of scope? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the refusal of the turn-off command from a worker kept as a requirement, not only as a scenario? [Consistency, Spec §US3 Scenario 3, §FR-007]

## Path safety of the session id

- [ ] CHK008 Is the allowed character set for a session id stated exactly, with the result for an id outside it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK009 Is it stated where the id check happens: at every point that makes, reads or removes an entry, including on a saved machine? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Are symlink rules stated for both the folder and an entry, for make, read and remove? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the case of an empty or missing session id covered for turn-on and for the readers? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Saved machines over ssh

- [ ] CHK012 Is the saved-machine write of an entry at `start --autonomous` stated with the same layout and rules as the local one? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the per-machine output lines of turn-off (removed, not there, failed with reason) stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the case of two sessions on the same saved machine, one turning off, covered? [Coverage, Spec §US2 Scenario 2]

## Two sessions at the same time

- [ ] CHK015 Is the "same moment" case stated as a measurable result (neither changes the other), not only as an intent? [Measurability, Spec §US1 Scenario 5, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 Is it clear that two sessions in the same worktree are also covered, not only two worktrees? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the result stated when an old single-file flag is present and a second session turns on while a first runs an older version? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-008]

## Turn-off triggers

- [ ] CHK018 Are all three turn-off triggers (task finished, "stop autonomous", continue later) listed in one requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the order "turn off, then write the handoff" stated, and what happens when the handoff runs in a background fork? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the crashed-session entry stated as an accepted leftover with its effect bounded to its own id? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, §Assumptions]

## Tests

- [ ] CHK021 Does each of the three test files have a stated two-session, two-worktree case, and is the turn-off-one case placed in a named file? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK022 Is "changed only where they name the old layout" clear enough to tell an allowed test change from a weakened test? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
